babs.23: The Prophet ﷺ urging the delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays to preserve faith and knowledge
babs.24: Travelling for a question that has arisen, and teaching one's family
babs.25: Taking turns in attending for knowledge
babs.26: Anger in admonition and teaching on seeing something disliked

babs.29: A man teaching his slave-woman and his family

babs.33: Whether a separate day is set for women for knowledge

babs.44: Asking and giving rulings while stoning the Jamarāt

babs.51: One who answers the questioner with more than he asked

59.matn: Muḥammad ibn Sinān narrated to us, he said: Fulaiḥ narrated to us, (change of chain) and Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mundhir narrated to me, he said: Muḥammad ibn Fulaiḥ narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: Hilāl ibn ʿAlī narrated to me, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Abū Huraira, he said: While the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was speaking to the people in a gathering, a Bedouin came to him and said: “When is the Hour?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went on speaking. Some of the people said: “He heard what he said and disliked it.” Others said: “No, he did not hear it.” When he had finished his talk, he said: “Where is – I think – the one who asked about the Hour?” He said: “Here I am, O Messenger of Allah.” He said: “When the trust (al-amāna) is lost, then await the Hour.” He said: “How is it lost?” He said: “When authority is entrusted to those not fit for it, then await the Hour.”
59.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who is asked about knowledge while occupied with his talk”. It is derived from it that the teacher may finish his talk before answering. In content, the hadith names the loss of trustworthiness, especially in the assignment of offices, as a sign of the Hour.

60.matn: Abū n-Nuʿmān ʿĀrim ibn al-Faḍl narrated to us, he said: Abū ʿAwāna narrated to us, from Abū Bishr, from Yūsuf ibn Māhak, from ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAmr, he said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, fell behind us on a journey we made. Then he caught up with us while (the time of) the prayer was pressing us and we were performing ablution. We began to (merely) wipe over our feet. So he called out at the top of his voice: “Woe to the heels from the Fire!” – two or three times.
60.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who raises his voice in (teaching) knowledge”. The hadith shows that the feet must be washed completely in ablution, and that repetition and calling out loudly can be appropriate in teaching.

61.matn: Qutaiba narrated to us, Ismāʿīl ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, from ʿAbdallāh ibn Dīnār, from Ibn ʿUmar, he said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Among the trees there is a tree whose leaves do not fall, and it is like the Muslim. Tell me which it is.” The people thought of the trees of the desert. ʿAbdallāh said: It occurred to me that it was the date palm, but I felt shy (to say it). Then they said: “Tell us which it is, O Messenger of Allah.” He said: “It is the date palm.”
61.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī brings the hadith in the chapter on knowledge; it shows posing questions as a teaching method. The palm resembles the Muslim in its constant benefit. Ibn ʿUmar’s restraint shows the courtesy of the younger towards the elders.

62.matn: Khālid ibn Makhlad narrated to us, Sulaimān narrated to us, ʿAbdallāh ibn Dīnār narrated to us, from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he said: “Among the trees there is a tree whose leaves do not fall, and it is like the Muslim. Tell me which it is.” He said: The people thought of the trees of the desert. ʿAbdallāh said: It occurred to me that it was the date palm. Then they said: “Tell us which it is, O Messenger of Allah.” He said: “It is the date palm.”
62.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The imam poses a question to his companions to test their knowledge”. Testing questions stimulate reflection and consolidate what has been learned.

62.2.matn: Muḥammad ibn Salām narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Wāsiṭī narrated to us, from ʿAuf, from al-Ḥasan, he said: There is no harm in reading (the text) to the scholar. And Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf al-Firabrī informed us, and Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl al-Bukhārī narrated to us, he said: ʿUbaidallāh ibn Mūsā narrated to us, from Sufyān, he said: When (a text) is read to the narrator, there is no harm in (the listener) saying: “He narrated to me.” He said: And I heard Abū ʿĀṣim say, from Mālik and Sufyān: Reading to the scholar and his own reading are the same.
62.2.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Not a prophetic saying but statements of early scholars in the chapter on knowledge. They attest the method of reading to the teacher (ʿarḍ), which in hadith transmission was recognized as equivalent to hearing from the teacher.

63.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: al-Laith narrated to us, from Saʿīd – he is al-Maqburī –, from Sharīk ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn Abī Namir, that he heard Anas ibn Mālik say: While we were sitting with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the mosque, a man came in on a camel. He made it kneel in the mosque and tied it. Then he said to them: “Which of you is Muḥammad?” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was reclining among them. We said: “This fair-skinned man who is reclining.” The man said to him: “Son of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib!” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “I have answered you.” The man said to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “I am going to ask you and be severe with you in my questioning, so do not hold it against me.” He said: “Ask whatever occurs to you.” He said: “I ask you by your Lord and the Lord of those before you: has Allah sent you to all people?” He said: “O Allah, yes.” He said: “I adjure you by Allah: has Allah commanded you that we pray the five prayers in the day and night?” He said: “O Allah, yes.” He said: “I adjure you by Allah: has Allah commanded you that we fast this month of the year?” He said: “O Allah, yes.” He said: “I adjure you by Allah: has Allah commanded you to take this ṣadaqa from our rich and distribute it among our poor?” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “O Allah, yes.” Then the man said: “I believe in what you have brought, and I am the messenger of those of my people who are behind me. I am Ḍimām ibn Thaʿlaba, of the Banū Saʿd ibn Bakr.” Mūsā and ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd narrated it from Sulaimān, from Thābit, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, likewise.
63.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī brings the hadith in the chapter on knowledge and reading to the scholar: Ḍimām put before the Prophet ﷺ what he had heard, had it confirmed and conveyed it to his people. The hadith also shows the Prophet’s ﷺ patience with the questioner’s blunt manner.

64.matn: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbdallāh narrated to us, he said: Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd narrated to me, from Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUbaidallāh ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUtba ibn Masʿūd, that ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAbbās informed him: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent a man with his letter and ordered him to hand it to the chief of Baḥrain. The chief of Baḥrain handed it to Chosroes. When he had read it, he tore it up. (Ibn Shihāb said:) I think Ibn al-Musayyab said: So the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, invoked (Allah) against them that they be torn apart completely.
64.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter on handing over (munāwala) and scholars writing knowledge to other lands. It shows that written transmission is a recognized form of conveying.

65.matn: Muḥammad ibn Muqātil Abū l-Ḥasan narrated to us, ʿAbdallāh informed us, he said: Shuʿba informed us, from Qatāda, from Anas ibn Mālik, he said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wrote a letter – or wanted to write –, and it was said to him: “They do not read a letter unless it is sealed.” So he took a signet ring of silver, whose engraving was: “Muḥammad Rasūl Allāh”. It is as if I am looking at its whiteness on his hand. I (Shuʿba) said to Qatāda: “Who said that its engraving was ‘Muḥammad Rasūl Allāh’?” He said: “Anas.”
65.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: In the same chapter, the hadith shows care in written transmission so that it would be accepted by the recipient. The question at the end shows the precision of the narrators.

66.matn: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Mālik narrated to me, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, that Abū Murra, the client of ʿAqīl ibn Abī Ṭālib, informed him from Abū Wāqid al-Laithī: While the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was sitting in the mosque with the people around him, three men came. Two came towards the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and one went away. He said: The two stopped by the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. One of them saw a gap in the circle and sat in it; the other sat behind them; and the third turned away and left. When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, finished, he said: “Shall I not tell you about the three men? One of them sought refuge with Allah, so Allah gave him refuge. The other was shy, so Allah was shy of him. And the other turned away, so Allah turned away from him.”
66.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who sits where the gathering ends”. The hadith encourages attending gatherings of knowledge and filling gaps, and warns against turning away without reason.

67.matn: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Bishr narrated to us, he said: Ibn ʿAun narrated to us, from Ibn Sīrīn, from ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakra, from his father: He mentioned the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: He sat on his camel, and a man held its halter or rein. He said: “What day is this?” We kept silent until we thought he would give it a name other than its name. He said: “Is it not the Day of Sacrifice?” We said: “Yes.” He said: “And what month is this?” We kept silent until we thought he would give it another name. He said: “Is it not Dhū l-Ḥijja?” We said: “Yes.” He said: “Your blood, your property and your honour are sacred to you among yourselves, like the sanctity of this day of yours, in this month of yours, in this land of yours. Let the one present convey it to the one absent, for perhaps the one present will convey it to someone who will retain it better than he.”
67.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter on the Prophet’s ﷺ saying “Many a one to whom something is conveyed retains it better than the one who heard it”. The questions served to heighten attention and to emphasize the importance of what followed.

68.matn: Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Sufyān informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Wāʾil, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to give us admonition at intervals over the days, out of dislike that weariness should come upon us.”
68.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter on how the Prophet ﷺ gave them admonition and knowledge at intervals so they would not be put off. The hadith shows consideration for the listeners’ capacity, so that admonition remains effective.

69.matn: Muḥammad ibn Bashshār narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, he said: Abū al-Tayyāḥ narrated to me, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he said: “Make things easy and do not make them difficult, and give good tidings and do not drive people away.”
69.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: The same section: the hadith states the method of teaching and calling: make things easy rather than hard, and encourage rather than alienate.

70.matn: ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shayba narrated to us, he said: Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Abū Wāʾil, he said: “ʿAbdallāh used to remind the people every Thursday. A man said to him: O Abū ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān, I wish you would remind us every day. He said: What keeps me from that is that I dislike wearying you. I give you admonition at intervals as the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to give it to us, for fear of weariness coming upon us.”
70.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the report under the chapter “One who sets fixed days for the people of knowledge”. Ibn Masʿūd followed the Prophet’s ﷺ practice and chose Thursday; he declined a daily reminder so as not to cause boredom.

71.matn: Saʿīd ibn ʿUfayr narrated to us, he said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, from Yūnus, from Ibn Shihāb, he said: Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān said: I heard Muʿāwiya speaking as a preacher, saying: I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: “When Allah wills good for someone, He gives him understanding of the religion. I am only a distributor, and Allah is the One who gives. This community will continue to stand firm upon the command of Allah; those who oppose them will not harm them until the command of Allah comes.”
71.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “When Allah wills good for someone, He gives him understanding of the religion”. Understanding of the religion is a sign of intended good. The hadith also states that the Prophet ﷺ only distributes while Allah gives, and that a group of the community will remain upon Allah’s command.

72.matn: ʿAlī narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abī Najīḥ said to me, from Mujāhid, he said: “I accompanied Ibn ʿUmar to Medina and I did not hear him narrate from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, except a single hadith. He said: We were with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when some palm-heart (jummār) was brought. He said: Among the trees there is a tree that is like the Muslim. I wanted to say: It is the date palm. But I was the youngest of the people, so I kept silent. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: It is the date palm.”
72.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places this route under the chapter “Understanding in knowledge”. Ibn ʿUmar understood that the date palm was meant – the palm-heart that had been brought also pointed to it – but he remained silent because he was the youngest. It is another chain of the same parable as in nos. 61 and 62.

73.matn: Al-Ḥumaydī narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, he said: Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid narrated to me – in a way other than how al-Zuhrī narrated it to us –, he said: I heard Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim, he said: I heard ʿAbdallāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no envy except in two (things): a man whom Allah has given wealth and enabled to spend it in the truth, and a man whom Allah has given wisdom, and he judges by it and teaches it.”
73.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter on rightful aspiration (ightibāṭ) for knowledge and wisdom. Envy here means the permitted wish to have the like of a blessing without wanting it taken from the other. The two cases are spending wealth in the truth and judging and teaching with wisdom. Sufyān notes that Ismāʿīl’s route differs from that of al-Zuhrī.

74.matn: Muḥammad ibn Ghurayr al-Zuhrī narrated to me, he said: Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to me, from Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn Shihāb, he narrated that ʿUbaydallāh ibn ʿAbdallāh informed him, from Ibn ʿAbbās: “He disputed with al-Ḥurr ibn Qays ibn Ḥiṣn al-Fazārī about the companion of Mūsā. Ibn ʿAbbās said: He is al-Khidr. Then Ubayy ibn Kaʿb passed by them. Ibn ʿAbbās called him and said: I have disputed with this companion of mine about the companion of Mūsā, whom Mūsā asked for a way to meet. Did you hear the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, mention his affair? He said: Yes, I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: While Mūsā was in an assembly of the Children of Israel, a man came to him and said: Do you know anyone more knowledgeable than you? Mūsā said: No. Then Allah revealed to Mūsā: Rather, Our servant al-Khidr. So Mūsā asked for a way to him, and Allah made the fish a sign for him, and it was said to him: When you lose the fish, turn back, for you will meet him. He was following the trace of the fish in the sea. Then his servant said to Mūsā: ﴿Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? I forgot the fish, and none but Satan made me forget to mention it.﴾ ﴿He said: That is what we were seeking. So they went back, retracing their tracks.﴾ Then they found al-Khidr, and there occurred between them that which Allah, the Exalted, has related in His Book.”
74.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter on rightful aspiration for knowledge and wisdom. Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥurr disputed about the companion of Mūsā; Ubayy ibn Kaʿb confirmed from the Prophet ﷺ that it was al-Khidr. The account shows that Mūsā set out to seek someone of greater knowledge.

75.matn: Abū Maʿmar narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Wārith narrated to us, he said: Khālid narrated to us, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, drew me close to himself and said: O Allah, teach him the Book.”
75.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter on the Prophet’s ﷺ saying “O Allah, teach him the Book”. It is a supplication for Ibn ʿAbbās, connected with his later distinction in understanding the Book.

76.matn: Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Uways narrated to us, he said: Mālik narrated to me, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUbaydallāh ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUtba, from ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAbbās, he said: “I came riding on a she-donkey, and I had at that time nearly reached puberty. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was praying at Minā, with no wall in front of him. I passed in front of part of the row, let the she-donkey graze, and entered the row, and that was not objected to in my regard.”
76.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “When a child’s hearing is valid”. Ibn ʿAbbās was close to puberty, and his report of what he witnessed was accepted; the incident also shows that his passing in front of part of the row was not reproved then.

77.matn: Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf narrated to me, he said: Abū Mushir narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Ḥarb narrated to me, al-Zubaydī narrated to me, from al-Zuhrī, from Maḥmūd ibn al-Rabīʿ, he said: “I remember from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, a mouthful of water that he sprayed in my face, when I was five years old, from a bucket.”
77.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the report under the same chapter on when a child’s hearing is valid. Maḥmūd was five years old and remembered a specific act of the Prophet ﷺ; this is cited as evidence that a young child’s hearing can be valid if he retains it reliably.

78.matn: Abū al-Qāsim Khālid ibn Khalī narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, he said: al-Awzāʿī said: al-Zuhrī informed us, from ʿUbaydallāh ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUtba ibn Masʿūd, from Ibn ʿAbbās: “He disputed with al-Ḥurr ibn Qays ibn Ḥiṣn al-Fazārī about the companion of Mūsā. Then Ubayy ibn Kaʿb passed by them. Ibn ʿAbbās called him and said: I have disputed with this companion of mine about the companion of Mūsā, who asked for a way to meet him. Did you hear the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, mention his affair? Ubayy said: Yes, I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, mention his affair, saying: While Mūsā was in an assembly of the Children of Israel, a man came to him and said: Do you know anyone more knowledgeable than you? Mūsā said: No. Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed to Mūsā: Rather, Our servant al-Khidr. So he asked for a way to meet him, and Allah made the fish a sign for him, and it was said to him: When you lose the fish, turn back, for you will meet him. Mūsā, peace be upon him, was following the trace of the fish in the sea. Then the servant of Mūsā said to Mūsā: ﴿Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? I forgot the fish, and none but Satan made me forget to mention it.﴾ Mūsā said: ﴿That is what we were seeking. So they went back, retracing their tracks.﴾ Then they found al-Khidr, and there occurred between them what Allah has related in His Book.”
78.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places this route under the chapter “Going out in search of knowledge”. It is another chain of the account of Mūsā and al-Khidr: Mūsā, peace be upon him, went out to find him. The wording differs in details from no. 74; the honorific with Mūsā appears only on this route.

79.matn: Muḥammad ibn al-ʿAlāʾ narrated to us, he said: Ḥammād ibn Usāma narrated to us, from Burayd ibn ʿAbdallāh, from Abū Burda, from Abū Mūsā, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he said: “The likeness of what Allah has sent me with of guidance and knowledge is that of abundant rain that falls on a land. Part of it was pure soil and accepted the water, so it brought forth much herbage and grass. Part of it was hard ground and held the water; Allah made people benefit by it, so they drank, watered, and cultivated. And another part of it was only barren plains that neither hold water nor bring forth herbage. That is the likeness of one who gains understanding in the religion of Allah and is benefited by what Allah has sent me with, so he learns and teaches; and the likeness of one who does not raise his head at that and does not accept the guidance of Allah with which I was sent.” Abū ʿAbdallāh said: Isḥāq said: “And among it was a portion that ‘qīlat’ the water.” A qāʿ is level ground that water covers, and al-ṣafṣaf is the flat, even land.
79.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The virtue of one who learns and teaches”. The parable divides people by their response to revelation: those who absorb, learn and teach; those who hold the water and benefit others; and those who neither retain nor bear fruit. The closing note is a scholar’s remark: Abū ʿAbdallāh – al-Bukhārī – reports a wording variant and a lexical explanation from Isḥāq.

80.matn: ʿImrān ibn Maysara narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Wārith narrated to us, from Abū al-Tayyāḥ, from Anas, he said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Among the signs of the Hour is that knowledge will be taken away, ignorance will be established, wine will be drunk, and fornication will appear.”
80.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The taking away of knowledge and the spread of ignorance”. The removal of knowledge is counted among the signs of the Hour, together with the spread of ignorance and of open sins.

81.matn: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿba, from Qatāda, from Anas, he said: I will narrate to you a hadith that no one will narrate to you after me. I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: “Among the signs of the Hour is that knowledge will decrease, ignorance will appear, fornication will appear, women will become many and men few, until one guardian will be for fifty women.”
81.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī also places this route under the same chapter on the taking away of knowledge. Anas stresses that he heard the hadith himself. The numerical predominance of women is mentioned in addition.

82.matn: Saʿīd ibn ʿUfayr narrated to us, he said: al-Layth narrated to me, he said: ʿAqīl narrated to me, from Ibn Shihāb, from Ḥamza ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUmar, that Ibn ʿUmar said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: “While I was asleep, a cup of milk was brought to me. I drank until I could see the quenching coming out in my nails. Then I gave my remainder to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.” They said: “How did you interpret it, O Messenger of Allah?” He said: “Knowledge.”
82.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The virtue of knowledge”. In the dream the milk is interpreted as knowledge; giving the remainder to ʿUmar points to his share in it, without requiring a ranking beyond what the text itself states.

83.matn: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Mālik narrated to me, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿĪsā ibn Ṭalḥa ibn ʿUbaydallāh, from ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood at Minā during the Farewell Pilgrimage, and the people were asking him. A man came to him and said: I did not realize, and I shaved before I slaughtered. He said: Slaughter, and there is no harm. Another came and said: I did not realize, and I slaughtered before I stoned. He said: Stone, and there is no harm. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was not asked about anything done earlier or later without saying: Do it, and there is no harm.”
83.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Giving a ruling while standing on a mount or the like”. The Prophet ﷺ gave rulings at Minā while standing; to those who had brought a rite of the pilgrimage forward or delayed it, he said there was no harm.

84.matn: Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Wuḥayb narrated to us, he said: Ayyūb narrated to us, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was asked during his pilgrimage. Someone said: I slaughtered before I stoned? He gestured with his hand and said: And there is no harm. Someone said: I shaved before I slaughtered? He gestured with his hand: And there is no harm.”
84.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who answers a question with a gesture of the hand or head”. The same matter as in no. 83 is answered here by a gesture of the hand.

85.matn: Al-Makkī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, he said: Ḥanẓala ibn Abī Sufyān informed us, from Sālim, he said: I heard Abū Huraira, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he said: “Knowledge will be taken away, ignorance and trials will appear, and al-harj will increase.” It was said: “O Messenger of Allah, what is al-harj?” He said: “Like this,” with his hand, and he turned it, as if he meant killing.
85.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who answers a question with a gesture of the hand or head”. Asked what al-harj was, the Prophet ﷺ answered with a hand gesture understood as killing. The hadith also belongs thematically to the taking away of knowledge.

86.matn: Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Wuḥayb narrated to us, he said: Hishām narrated to us, from Fāṭima, from Asmāʾ, she said: “I came to ʿĀʾisha while she was praying and said: What is the matter with the people? She pointed to the sky, and behold, the people were standing. She said: Glory be to Allah. I said: A sign? She nodded with her head: Yes. I stood until faintness overcame me, and I began to pour water over my head. Then the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, praised Allah, the Exalted, and extolled Him, then said: There is nothing I had not been shown except that I saw it in my standing-place, even the Garden and the Fire. It was revealed to me that you will be tried in your graves, like or nearly – I do not know which of those Asmāʾ said – the trial of the false messiah (al-Masīḥ al-Dajjāl). It will be said: What do you know of this man? As for the believer, or the one with certainty – I do not know which of the two Asmāʾ said – he will say: He is Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah, he came to us with the clear signs and the guidance, we answered and followed, he is Muḥammad, three times. Then it will be said: Sleep as a righteous one; we have known that you were certain of him. As for the hypocrite, or the doubter – I do not know which of those Asmāʾ said – he will say: I do not know; I heard the people saying something, so I said it.”
86.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter on answering with a gesture of the hand or head: ʿĀʾisha answered during the prayer by pointing and nodding. The hadith describes the trial in the grave; at certain points Asmāʾ notes that she was unsure which exact wording was used. That uncertainty is reported as her own reservation, not as a later addition.

87.matn: Muḥammad ibn Bashshār narrated to us, he said: Ghundar narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Abū Jamra, he said: “I used to interpret between Ibn ʿAbbās and the people. He said: The delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He said: Who is the delegation, or: who are the people? They said: Rabīʿa. He said: Welcome to the people, or: to the delegation, neither disgraced nor remorseful. They said: We come to you from a far distance, and between us and you is this tribe of the unbelievers of Muḍar, and we cannot come to you except in a sacred month. So command us with a matter that we may inform those behind us of, and by which we may enter the Garden. He commanded them with four and forbade them four; he commanded them to have faith in Allah, the Exalted, alone. He said: Do you know what faith in Allah alone is? They said: Allah and His Messenger know best. He said: The testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing the prayer, giving the zakāt, fasting Ramaḍān, and that you give the fifth of the spoils. And he forbade them al-dubbāʾ (gourd vessels), al-ḥantam, and al-muzaffat (pitch-coated vessels). Shuʿba said: Sometimes he said: al-naqīr. And sometimes he said: al-muqayyar. He said: Memorize it and inform those behind you.”
87.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter on the Prophet ﷺ urging the delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays to preserve faith and knowledge. They were to retain what they heard and pass it on. The forbidden vessel types are named as transmitted; Shuʿba notes variation in one of the names. That is a remark of the narrator.

88.matn: Muḥammad ibn Muqātil Abū l-Ḥasan narrated to us, he said: ʿAbdallāh informed us, he said: ʿUmar ibn Saʿīd ibn Abī Ḥusayn informed us, he said: ʿAbdallāh ibn Abī Mulayka narrated to me, from ʿUqba ibn al-Ḥārith: “He married a daughter of Abū Ihāb ibn ʿAzīz. Then a woman came to him and said: I suckled ʿUqba and the one he has married. ʿUqba said to her: I do not know that you suckled me, and you did not inform me. So he rode to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in Medina and asked him. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: How, when it has already been said? So ʿUqba parted from her, and she married another husband.”
88.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Travelling for a question that has arisen, and teaching one's family”. ʿUqba travelled to Medina specifically to ask about the report of suckling. The Prophet ﷺ treated the statement already made as sufficient for the marriage not to remain.

89.matn: Abū al-Yamān narrated to us, Shuʿayb informed us, from al-Zuhrī (change of chain). Abū ʿAbdallāh said: And Ibn Wahb said: Yūnus informed us, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUbaydallāh ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn Abī Thawr, from ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿUmar, he said: “I and a neighbor of mine from the Anṣār were among Banū Umayya ibn Zayd, which is part of the ʿAwālī of Medina. We used to take turns going down to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: he would go down one day, and I would go down one day. When I went down I would bring him the news of that day of revelation and other matters; and when he went down he would do the like. My Ansārī companion went down on his turn, knocked hard on my door and said: Is he there? I was alarmed, went out to him, and he said: A great matter has occurred. He said: I went in to Ḥafṣa, and she was weeping. I said: Has the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, divorced you? She said: I do not know. Then I went in to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and I said while standing: Have you divorced your wives? He said: No. I said: Allah is greatest.”
89.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the report under the chapter “Taking turns in attending for knowledge”. ʿUmar and his Ansārī neighbor alternated so as not to miss any of the revelation, and they taught one another. The opening of the first chain breaks off at the change-of-chain mark; Abū ʿAbdallāh – al-Bukhārī – adds Ibn Wahb’s route, which carries the text.

90.matn: Muḥammad ibn Kathīr narrated to us, he said: Sufyān informed us, from Ibn Abī Khālid, from Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim, from Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī, he said: “A man said: O Messenger of Allah, I can hardly catch the prayer because so-and-so prolongs it for us. I never saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, more angry in an admonition than on that day. He said: O people, you are driving people away. Whoever leads the people in prayer should make it light, for among them is the sick, the weak, and the one who has a need.”
90.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Anger in admonition and teaching on seeing something disliked”. The anger was at driving the congregation away by unduly long leading of the prayer, not at a personal attack.

91.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, he said: Abū ʿĀmir narrated to us, he said: Sulaymān ibn Bilāl al-Madīnī narrated to us, from Rabīʿa ibn Abī ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān, from Yazīd, the client of al-Munbaʿith, from Zayd ibn Khālid al-Juhanī: “A man asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about lost property. He said: Know its tie – or he said: its vessel – and its wrapping, then announce it for a year, then enjoy it. If its owner comes, give it back to him. He said: And a stray camel? He became angry until his cheeks flushed – or he said: his face flushed. He said: What have you to do with it? It has its water-skin and its hooves; it goes to water and grazes the trees. Leave it until its owner finds it. He said: And a stray sheep? He said: It is for you, or for your brother, or for the wolf.”
91.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter on anger in admonition when something disliked is seen. The anger was at the question about the stray camel, which can fend for itself and is therefore not treated like ordinary lost property. The narrator’s uncertainty about certain words is preserved.

92.matn: Muḥammad ibn al-ʿAlāʾ narrated to us, he said: Abū Usāma narrated to us, from Burayd, from Abū Burda, from Abū Mūsā, he said: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was asked about things he disliked. When they pressed him too much he became angry, then said to the people: Ask me about whatever you wish. A man said: Who is my father? He said: Your father is Ḥudhāfa. Another stood up and said: Who is my father, O Messenger of Allah? He said: Your father is Sālim, the client of Shayba. When ʿUmar saw what was in his face he said: O Messenger of Allah, we repent to Allah, the Exalted.”
92.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter on anger in admonition. The anger arose when the questions became excessive; ʿUmar broke off when he saw what was in the Prophet’s ﷺ face, and declared repentance to Allah.

93.matn: Abū al-Yamān narrated to us, he said: Shuʿayb informed us, from al-Zuhrī, he said: Anas ibn Mālik informed me: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out. Then ʿAbdallāh ibn Ḥudhāfa stood up and said: Who is my father? He said: Your father is Ḥudhāfa. Then he kept saying: Ask me. So ʿUmar knelt on his knees and said: We are pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muḥammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as prophet. Then he became silent.”
93.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who kneels before the imam or the narrator”. ʿUmar knelt in order to end the excessive questions, and declared his satisfaction with Allah, with Islam and with the Prophet ﷺ.

94.matn: ʿAbda narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, he said: ʿAbdallāh ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, he said: Thumāma ibn ʿAbdallāh narrated to us, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: that he, “when he gave the greeting of peace, gave it three times, and when he spoke a word, he repeated it three times.”
94.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who repeats his words three times to be understood”. The repetition was for understanding and retention, not mere habit.

95.matn: ʿAbda ibn ʿAbdallāh narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, he said: ʿAbdallāh ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, he said: Thumāma ibn ʿAbdallāh narrated to us, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, “that when he spoke a word he repeated it three times until it was understood from him, and when he came upon a people and greeted them, he greeted them three times.”
95.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: This is another route of the same hadith: it is stated explicitly that the threefold repetition was for understanding, and that the greeting of peace when coming upon a group was given three times.

96.matn: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Abū ʿAwāna narrated to us, from Abū Bishr, from Yūsuf ibn Māhak, from ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAmr, he said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, lagged behind on a journey we travelled. Then he caught up with us when the prayer, the afternoon prayer, had already pressed upon us, and we were performing the ablution. We began wiping over our feet. He called out at the top of his voice: Woe to the heels from the Fire. Twice or three times.”
96.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the same chapter on repeating three times. The warning about heels left incompletely washed was called out two or three times so that it would be understood and retained.

97.matn: Muḥammad, that is Ibn Salām, informed us, al-Muḥāribī narrated to us, he said: Ṣāliḥ ibn Ḥayyān narrated to us, he said: ʿĀmir al-Shaʿbī said: Abū Burda narrated to me, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Three have two rewards: a man of the People of the Book who believed in his prophet and believed in Muḥammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace; the owned slave when he fulfills the right of Allah and the right of his masters; and a man who had a slave-woman, disciplined her and did so well, taught her and did so well, then freed her and married her: he has two rewards.” Then ʿĀmir said: “We have given it to you for nothing; people used to ride to Medina for less than this.”
97.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “A man teaching his slave-woman and his family”. The third case shows the reward for teaching well, then freeing and marrying. The close is a remark of ʿĀmir al-Shaʿbī to the listener, stressing the value of a hadith obtained without travel.

98.matn: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Ayyūb, he said: I heard ʿAṭāʾ, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I bear witness concerning the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace – or ʿAṭāʾ said: I bear witness concerning Ibn ʿAbbās –: “that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out, and with him was Bilāl. He thought that he had not been heard, so he admonished them and commanded them to give charity. The woman would throw down her earring and her ring, and Bilāl would take (them) in the edge of his garment.” Ismāʿīl said, from Ayyūb, from ʿAṭāʾ, and he said from Ibn ʿAbbās: I bear witness concerning the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.
98.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter on the imam admonishing and teaching the women. The Prophet ﷺ turned to the women specifically. The uncertainty whether ʿAṭāʾ said “I bear witness concerning the Prophet” or “concerning Ibn ʿAbbās” is kept; Ismāʿīl’s appended remark supports the wording “concerning the Prophet” and is marked as a scholar’s note.

99.matn: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿAbdallāh narrated to us, he said: Sulaymān narrated to me, from ʿAmr ibn Abī ʿAmr, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Saʿīd al-Maqburī, from Abū Huraira, that he said: “It was said: O Messenger of Allah, who is the happiest of people with your intercession on the Day of Resurrection? The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: I had thought, O Abū Huraira, that no one would ask me about this hadith before you, because of the eagerness for hadith I have seen in you. The happiest of people with my intercession on the Day of Resurrection is the one who says there is no god but Allah, sincerely from his heart – or: from his self.”
99.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Eagerness for ḥadīth”. The Prophet ﷺ singles out Abū Huraira’s eagerness. The intercession is here tied to the sincere testimony; the uncertainty “heart or self” is the narrator’s.

99.2.matn: Al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muslim narrated to us, from ʿAbdallāh ibn Dīnār, with that, meaning the report of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz up to his words: the passing away of the scholars.
99.2.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: No prophetic saying in this entry, but a shortened supporting chain. It refers to the report of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz up to the words about the passing away of the scholars; the full wording of that report is not in this corpus entry. The item belongs to the chapter on how knowledge is taken away, and prepares no. 100.

100.matn: Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Uways narrated to us, he said: Mālik narrated to me, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: “Allah does not take away knowledge by wresting it from the servants, but He takes away knowledge by taking away the scholars, until, when no scholar remains, the people take ignorant heads. They are asked and give rulings without knowledge, so they go astray and lead others astray.”
100.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “How knowledge is taken away”. Knowledge disappears chiefly through the passing of the scholars, not by being suddenly torn from people’s hearts. One who gives rulings without knowledge harms himself and others.

101.matn: Ādam narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, he said: Ibn al-Aṣbahānī narrated to me, he said: I heard Abū Ṣāliḥ Dhakwān narrating from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī: “The women said to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: The men have got the better of us with you, so appoint for us a day of your own. He promised them a day on which he met them, admonished them and instructed them. Among what he said to them was: There is no woman among you who sends ahead three of her children but that they will be a screen for her from the Fire. A woman said: And two? He said: And two.”
101.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter on whether a separate day is set for women for knowledge. The Prophet ﷺ granted the request and taught them separately. The reward for children who have gone ahead is, in the text itself, extended to two.

102.matn: Muḥammad ibn Bashshār narrated to us, he said: Ghundar narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn al-Aṣbahānī, from Dhakwān, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with this (same sense). And from ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn al-Aṣbahānī, he said: I heard Abū Ḥāzim, from Abū Huraira, he said: “Three who have not yet reached the age of accountability.”
102.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Another route to no. 101, together with a short additional report from Abū Huraira: the three children had not yet reached the age of accountability (al-ḥinth). It is given as this route’s own brief wording, not as a rewritten full repetition of the hadith.

103.matn: Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam narrated to us, he said: Nāfiʿ ibn ʿUmar informed us, he said: Ibn Abī Mulayka narrated to me: that ʿĀʾisha, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would not hear anything she did not know without asking about it again until she knew it; and that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever is called to account will be punished.” ʿĀʾisha said: So I said: Does Allah the Exalted not say: “Then he will be given an easy reckoning”? She said: He said: That is only the presentation (al-ʿarḍ); but whoever is questioned closely about the reckoning will perish.
103.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who hears something and asks again until he understands it”. ʿĀʾisha would ask until the meaning was clear. The Prophet ﷺ distinguishes between the mere presentation of deeds and a close interrogation of the reckoning, which leads to ruin. The verse ʿĀʾisha cited is the well-known wording about an easy reckoning.

104.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: al-Layth narrated to me, he said: Saʿīd narrated to me, from Abū Shurayḥ, “that he said to ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd while he was sending troops to Mecca: Give me leave, O commander, to tell you a word with which the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood the morning after the Day of the Conquest. My ears heard it, my heart retained it, and my eyes saw him when he spoke it: He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: Allah made Mecca sacred; the people did not make it sacred. So it is not lawful for anyone who believes in Allah and the Last Day to shed blood therein, nor to cut down a tree therein. If anyone claims a concession because of the fighting of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, therein, then say: Allah permitted it to His Messenger and did not permit it to you. I was permitted it only for a part of a day, then its sanctity has returned today as it was yesterday. And let the one present convey it to the one absent. It was said to Abū Shurayḥ: What did ʿAmr say? He said: I know better than you, O Abū Shurayḥ. It does not shelter a sinner, nor one fleeing on account of blood, nor one fleeing with a khirba.”
104.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Let the one present convey the knowledge to the one absent”. Abū Shurayḥ cites the Prophet’s ﷺ address on the morning after the conquest of Mecca: its sanctity is from Allah, and the temporary leave to fight was only for the Messenger for part of a day. ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd’s reply is the governor’s statement, not a prophetic saying; khirba is commonly understood as theft or a crime.

105.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb narrated to us, he said: Ḥammād narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī Bakra, from Abū Bakra, he mentioned the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he said: “For your blood and your property – Muḥammad said: and I think he said: and your honor – are forbidden to you, like the sanctity of this day of yours, in this month of yours. Take heed: let the one present among you convey it to the one absent.” And Muḥammad used to say: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, spoke the truth; it was thus: ‘Have I conveyed?’, twice.”
105.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: The same chapter: the one present is to convey. Muḥammad’s uncertainty – in the chain usually Ibn Sīrīn – as to whether “your honor” was also mentioned is preserved. His addition “Have I conveyed?”, twice, is a remark of the narrator, not a separate prophetic chain in this entry.

106.matn: ʿAlī ibn al-Jaʿd narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba informed us, he said: Manṣūr informed me, he said: I heard Ribʿī ibn Ḥirāsh say: I heard ʿAlī say: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Do not lie about me, for whoever lies about me, let him enter the Fire.”
106.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “The sin of one who lies about the Prophet ﷺ”. The warning is general; nearby wordings in the following entries include lying deliberately.

107.matn: Abū al-Walīd narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Jāmiʿ ibn Shaddād, from ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbdallāh ibn al-Zubayr, from his father, he said: I said to al-Zubayr: “I do not hear you narrating from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as so-and-so and so-and-so narrate.” He said: “As for me, I did not leave him; but I heard him say: Whoever lies about me, let him take his seat in the Fire.”
107.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Zubayr gives this as the reason he narrated little, even though he did not leave the Prophet ﷺ. The warning itself was enough to make him hold back. No invented figures are added for the number of his hadiths.

108.matn: Abū Maʿmar narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Wārith narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, Anas said: What truly keeps me from narrating many hadiths to you is that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever deliberately fabricates a lie about me, let him take his seat in the Fire.”
108.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Anas gives the same reason for restraint; in this wording intent (taʿammud) is stated expressly. It belongs to the same chapter on the sin of lying about the Prophet ﷺ.
